next_step_summary: PR #234 records the product-owner decision to freeze the Surya/cloud OCR infrastructure track and move implementation focus to the Question Engine. The attempted targeted-region CPU runtime after merged PR #233 did not execute: Cloud Build source upload/API enablement completed, but build creation stopped at PERMISSION_DENIED before container build/deploy/OCR, so this is not evidence that Surya CPU performance failed. The freeze is a prioritization decision: scalable cloud OCR is not currently required for single-user product development, while Question Engine behavior is the higher-value product unknown. Reopen cloud/Surya infrastructure only when automatic OCR becomes a concrete blocker or real product usage justifies renewed infrastructure work. Tesseract full-page OCR remains NO-GO. Question Engine must remain OCR-provider-independent and start from a sanitized golden corpus derived from owner-controlled real rental contracts; persistent repository fixtures must contain no recoverable PII. Handwriting must not be semantically inferred or reconstructed; if meaning depends on handwriting, the system must surface that dependency rather than guess. Stable party-role placeholders must preserve contract directionality after de-identification. No runtime, provider, upload, masking, Gemini call, storage or production privacy claim is added by this state-only pivot.
